title: Punctured affine cone and finite homogeneous slice over a projective chart
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $V\ne0$ be finite-dimensional, and let $j:Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf P_{\mathrm{lines}}(V)$ be a closed immersion of $k$-schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion]. The projective space parametrizes lines. Put $P=\operatorname{Sym}_k(V^\vee)$, the graded commutative algebra freely generated by $V^\vee$ in degree one, and let $I\subset P$ be the homogeneous ideal of polynomials whose associated sections restrict to zero on $Y$. Write $C=\operatorname{Spec}(P/I)\subset\mathbf A(V)$ for the affine cone and $L=j^*\mathcal O(1)$ for the dual tautological invertible module [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-sc-invertible-module, def-pc-projective-space-twist]. There is a canonical isomorphism over $Y$ between $C\setminus\{0\}$ and the complement of the zero section in the total space of $L^{-1}$, taking a nonzero vector to its line; the total space of a line bundle is the scheme obtained by gluing $U\times\mathbf A^1$ using its linear transition functions. Let $f\in P$ be homogeneous of degree $d>0$ and let $c\in k^\times$. Set $Y_f=\{y:f|_Y(y)\ne0\}$ and $T=\operatorname{Spec}(P/(I,f-c))$. The vector-to-line map induces a finite locally free surjection $p:T\to Y_f$ of degree $d$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. These assertions allow empty $Y_f$, nonreduced $Y$, and characteristic dividing $d$. The construction is natural under linear automorphisms of $V$ preserving $Y$ and $f$.

source.place: Tag 01M4 (lemma-standard-open), standard homogeneous-localization charts; Tag 01NF (definition-projective-space), with O(-1) transition functions. The punctured-cone comparison and finite cyclic slice are an agent reconstruction from these charts; the explicit chart argument is in report.md.

proof.text: Choose a basis of $V^\vee$, writing $P=k[x_0,\ldots,x_n]$ with $n\geq0$, and put $S=P/I$ and $z_i=\overline{x_i}$. By [lem-sfb-projective-closed-subscheme-homogeneous-ideal], the ideal defined in the statement identifies $Y$ scheme-theoretically with $\operatorname{Proj}(S)$, also for nonreduced or empty $Y$. Thus [def-pc-proj] gives $U_i=Y\cap D_+(x_i)=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$, $A_i=(S_{z_i})_0$. These opens cover because the $z_i$ generate the positive-degree ideal. By [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts], $x_i|_Y$ freely generates $L$ on $U_i$, and $x_j|_Y=(z_j/z_i)x_i|_Y$ on that chart. The quotient-chart assertion [lem-sfb-homogeneous-quotient-chart-kernel] identifies $A_i$ with $k[u_j:j\ne i]/J_i$, where $u_j=x_j/x_i$ and $J_i$ is generated by the dehomogenizations $F/x_i^{\deg F}$ of homogeneous $F\in I$.

For each $i$ there is an explicit inverse pair $A_i[t_i,t_i^{-1}]\simeq S[1/z_i]$. In the forward direction send $t_i$ to $z_i$ and $u_j$ to $z_j/z_i$. For the inverse send $x_i$ to $t_i$, $x_j$ to $u_jt_i$, and $z_i^{-1}$ to $t_i^{-1}$. A homogeneous relation $F\in I$ maps to $t_i^{\deg F}F(1,u)=0$, by the description of $J_i$ in step 1; all relations of $I$ are sums of homogeneous ones. Conversely $F(1,u)$ maps to $F/z_i^{\deg F}=0$. These maps therefore descend, and their composites fix every displayed generator. This also proves the assertion if either ring is zero or $z_i$ is nilpotent; no cancellation by $z_i$ is used. The fraction operations are those of [def-weil-ring-localization-away].

source.place: Tags 03GL and 01M4, agent expansion: inverse ring maps on a degree-one cone chart

proof.text: The opens $D_C(z_i)=\operatorname{Spec}S[1/z_i]$ cover $C\setminus\{0\}$: the origin in the ambient affine space is cut out by all $x_i$. Step 2 identifies each with $U_i\times\mathbf G_m$, where $\mathbf G_m=\operatorname{Spec}k[t,t^{-1}]$. On the $i,j$ overlap the identities are $t_j=(z_j/z_i)t_i$ and $x_a/x_j=(x_a/x_i)/(x_j/x_i)$. Let $e_i$ be the frame of $L$ given by $x_i$, and $\epsilon_i$ its dual frame of $L^{-1}$. Since $e_j=(z_j/z_i)e_i$, one has $\epsilon_i=(z_j/z_i)\epsilon_j$. Thus a vector $t_i\epsilon_i=t_j\epsilon_j$ has exactly the same transition $t_j=(z_j/z_i)t_i$. By the definition of the total space in the item these are its gluing transitions. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] to the chart maps and to their inverses; the composites are the identity on every chart, hence globally. This proves the isomorphism over $Y$ and the vector-to-line projection.

source.place: Tags 01NG and 01MS (lemma-when-invertible), dual frames; scheme-map gluing as in Schemes Tag 01JA

proof.text: The isomorphism is canonical, despite choosing coordinates to construct it. For any nonzero linear form $\ell=\sum a_jx_j$, on its nonvanishing locus the same formulas give $t_\ell=\ell(v)=t_i\sum a_j(x_j/x_i)$ and the normalized vector $v/\ell(v)$. These formulas show directly that the constructions from any two bases agree on the intersections of their charts. Equality of the chart maps gives equality globally by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. For a linear automorphism $g$ preserving $Y$ scheme-theoretically, pullback preserves $I$ because it preserves the vanishing of restricted sections. Then the vector $v$ is sent to $gv$, and its line and tautological vector are sent to their corresponding images; the formulas just written commute with this substitution. If $g$ also preserves $f$, then $f(gv)=f(v)$, so this commutation restricts to the level $f=c$. This proves the requested naturality, including its restriction to the finite slice.

source.place: Tags 01NF (definition-projective-space) and 01NG; agent verification of independence and naturality by linear substitution

proof.text: Since $d>0$, $f$ belongs to $(x_0,\ldots,x_n)$; its image on $T$ is the unit $c$. Therefore the opens $D_T(x_i)$ cover $T$, so $T\subseteq C\setminus\{0\}$. On $U_i$ put $a_i=f/x_i^d\in A_i$ and $W_i=U_i\cap Y_f=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ with $B_i=A_i[1/a_i]$. Step 2 changes the level equation into $a_it_i^d=c$. In the Laurent quotient, $a_i$ is a unit with inverse $t_i^d/c$. Conversely in $B_i[t_i]/(t_i^d-c/a_i)$ the element $t_i$ is a unit, with inverse $(a_i/c)t_i^{d-1}$. The evident maps in both directions are inverse on coefficients and $t_i$. Hence $p^{-1}(W_i)=D_T(x_i)=\operatorname{Spec}E_i$, $E_i=B_i[t_i]/(t_i^d-c/a_i)$, with $p$ given by $B_i\to E_i$. These formulas also prove that the projection factors through $Y_f$, and that the $W_i$ cover it.

source.place: Tags 01M4 and 01MV (lemma-principal-open); agent expansion of the nonzero homogeneous level in a Laurent chart

proof.text: The polynomial $t_i^d-c/a_i$ is monic of degree $d$ whenever $B_i\ne0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free], $E_i$ has the $B_i$-basis $1,t_i,\ldots,t_i^{d-1}$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-free-algebra-spectrum] makes $\operatorname{Spec}E_i\to\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ finite, flat and locally of finite presentation. A zero $B_i$ gives an empty chart and imposes no condition; it can simply be omitted from the cover. For a point with residue field $K$ on a remaining chart, [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies its fibre algebra with $K\otimes_{B_i}E_i$. The basis above identifies this vector space with $K^d$: explicitly $\lambda\otimes\sum b_rt_i^r\mapsto(\lambda\overline b_r)_r$, with inverse $(\lambda_r)_r\mapsto\sum\lambda_r\otimes t_i^r$. Its dimension is $d$. This is precisely the degree clause of [def-pc-finite-locally-free].

source.place: Tag 02KB (lemma-finite-flat), affine finite-free case; monic division as in Algebra Tag 04GG; fibre rings in Schemes Tag 01I4

proof.text: Surjectivity can be checked on these same charts without extracting roots in $k$. For any $B_i$-module $M$, the displayed basis gives $E_i\otimes_{B_i}M\cong M^d$, by the coefficient and insertion formulas of step 6 with $M$ in place of $K$. Tensoring a complex with $E_i$ is therefore taking $d$ copies of it. Since $d>0$, exactness of the resulting complex is equivalent to exactness of the original one: kernels and images are coordinatewise, and the first coordinate tests the reverse implication. Thus $B_i\to E_i$ is faithfully flat by [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum] to obtain surjectivity on every $W_i$, and hence on $Y_f$.

source.place: Tags 00HB (definition-flat), faithfully flat exactness criterion, and 00HQ (lemma-ff-rings), faithfully flat implies surjective spectrum

proof.text: Each inclusion $W_i\hookrightarrow Y_f$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale], and the $W_i$ cover $Y_f$. The inverse images in step 5 are the corresponding base changes, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-locally-free-degree-etale-descent] applied to the degree-$d$ maps of step 6 proves that $p:T\to Y_f$ is finite locally free of degree $d$. Step 7 supplies surjectivity. If $Y_f$ is empty, step 5 makes every $D_T(x_i)$ empty and hence $T$ empty; the same descent statement applies to the empty cover. The calculations use homogeneous ideals and scheme quotients throughout, with no passage to radicals, so they retain nonreduced structure. They never divide by $d$ or assert etaleness of $p$; thus characteristic dividing $d$ is allowed.

source.place: Tag 02VO (lemma-descending-property-finite-locally-free), degree clause, applied to the open cover; open immersions are etale by Morphisms Tag 02GP
